articles.title: From missing India's original  squad to making history with silver, Roshibina Devi becomes first Indian woman to win three successive Asian Games medals
articles.summary: Naorem Roshibina Devi's Asian Games journey began with uncertainty but ended with another medal.
articles.body: Naorem Roshibina Devi's Asian Games journey began with uncertainty but ended with another medal. The 25-year-old Manipuri wushu player won silver in the women's 60kg Sanda category after losing 0-2 to China's Zhang Xiaoyu in the final at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall on Thursday.With the silver, Roshibina became the first Indian woman to win three successive Asian Games medals in wushu, following her bronze at Jakarta 2018 and silver at Hangzhou 2023.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyFrom controversy to the podiumRoshibina was not part of India's original squad after losing the selection trial to Divyanshi Choudhary in June. Divyanshi was initially selected but was later withdrawn after the Wushu Association of India said an MRI showed a partial high-grade ACL tear.Divyanshi had alleged that she was being mentally and physically harassed and claimed Roshibina had been involved. The WAI rejected the allegations and said the squad change was made on medical grounds. The Sports Ministry subsequently approved Roshibina as the replacement.Roshibina, who learnt about her inclusion around September 10, said she wanted to move on from the controversy."What happened was not because of me. It was the federation's decision. Whatever decision the federation (Wushu Association of India) took, I think it was a good decision," she said."I will ignore it (the accusation). I just want to focus on my goal."Little time to prepareRoshibina had been out of the national camp for around one-and-a-half months after losing the trials and travelled directly from Manipur after being recalled."There was a lot of disturbance when I came here for the Asian Games. I did not get much time to prepare. If I had more time, I would have done better," she said.Her coach Amit Pal also pointed to the lack of preparation, saying Roshibina had only limited training after being named in the team on September 10.Despite that, she defeated Bangladesh's Shika Khatun in the pre-quarterfinals and Macao, China's Chu Man Sin 5-0 in the quarterfinals before securing another Asian Games medal.Roshibina could not match Zhang's aggression and technical superiority in the gold-medal bout. The Chinese fighter won both rounds unanimously, with all five judges awarding her 5-0 decisions.Zhang dominated the scoring in both rounds, particularly with her side-kicks."She (Chinese player) is a new player, I have not fought against her. She was good in her side kicks. I also tried to defend. I tried to throw her, but she did better," Roshibina said.The silver left her disappointed at missing gold."I have won silver earlier and this time also, I could win only silver. I could not give the gold medal to the Indian people. I could not give what everyone wanted," she said.Born in Kwasiphai Mayai Leikai in Manipur's Bishnupur district, Roshibina's journey has also involved considerable family sacrifice, with her farmer father Naorem Damu Singh selling a piece of land to fund her training and travel in the early years.Now, with three successive Asian Games medals, Roshibina has another target."I want to inspire all the players. I want to be like them. I will do my best in the upcoming Games."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Aur achha ho sakta tha': Mairaj Ahmad Khan after Indian skeet team's record medal haul at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian skeet shooter Mairaj Ahmad Khan believes India's historic run of three medals in skeet at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has created a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian skeet shooter Mairaj Ahmad Khan believes India's historic run of three medals in skeet at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has created a strong platform for the Los Angeles Olympics. Mairaj, who was part of the men's skeet team that won bronze, felt India could have done better and believed the team had a chance to win gold.India won medals in all three skeet team events over two days, with the men's team, women's team and mixed team all finishing on the podium.For Mairaj, the men's team bronze was his first Asian Games medal. He had previously competed at the Asian Games in 2006, 2010 and 2014 before returning to the continental event in 2026.Mairaj already has three World Cup gold medals - in New Delhi in 2021, Changwon in 2022 and Cairo in 2023. He also has a silver from Rio de Janeiro in 2016 and a bronze from Cairo in 2021.Apart from this, he has one gold, two silver and three bronze medals at the Asian Championships.Looking back at his individual performance at the Asian Games, Mairaj felt tiredness also played a role."In the individual event, hunger was not there. I think I was a little tired. I was relaxed, mentally tired, overworked. Maybe the calendar is so busy," Mairaj told TimesofIndia.com from Japan.Mairaj felt the team could have finished with gold but said there would be more opportunities to improve, with the World Championships and Asian Championships coming up."Aur achha ho sakta tha. We could have won gold medal. The stage was set but no propblem, next time," Mairaj said about the team's bronze medal finish.Proud of Anantjeet and ParinaazMairaj was particularly pleased with the performances of Anantjeet and Parinaaz in the mixed team event. He said he was proud of the way the two shooters performed and saw their medal as part of a bigger process.The men's skeet team of Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Mairaj and Bhavtegh Singh Gill won bronze on Wednesday. The trio finished with 346 points and then prevailed over Kazakhstan in a shoot-off to secure third place.Later that day, Raiza Dhillon, Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Maheshwari Chauhan also won bronze in the women's team event, giving India its first-ever Asian Games medal in women's skeet.On Thursday, Anantjeet and Parinaaz added another bronze in the mixed team event, giving Indian skeet medals in all three team events."I am really proud of the way Anant and Parinaaz have performed. We are building a team together for LA Olympics," he said.'I will not stop'Mairaj was clear that the Asian Games medals are not the end of the journey.He said his focus remains on improving and continuing the fight for the Los Angeles Olympics. The dream of winning gold, he said, has not changed."I will not stop. Ever since I picked up the gun, I have felt that I could have done better. I have made some mistakes," he said."The fight is on for the LA Olympics. Gold was the dream and it will remain the dream," Mairaj said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs India at Asian Games: Anahat Singh to face Tanvi Khanna in squash quarterfinals
articles.summary: India enjoyed a strong day in squash at the Asian Games on Thursday as Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna, Abhay Singh and Veer Chotrani advanced to the singles
articles.body: India enjoyed a strong day in squash at the Asian Games on Thursday as Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna, Abhay Singh and Veer Chotrani advanced to the singles quarterfinals. Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar also booked their place in the mixed doubles quarterfinals in Aichi-Nagoya.Junior world champion Anahat began her women's singles campaign with a 3-0 (11-4, 11-5, 11-7) win over Singapore's Wai Iynn Au Yeong in just 19 minutes.Tanvi Khanna also moved into the last eight after defeating Singapore's Wai Yhann Au Yeong 3-1 (5-11, 11-4, 11-5, 13-11) in a 39-minute match.The two wins set up an all-Indian women's singles quarterfinal between Anahat and Tanvi.Unlike the previous edition, players who reach the semifinals are not guaranteed a medal in the singles competition. The two losing semifinalists will play a third-place playoff to decide the bronze medal.In the men's singles, Abhay Singh registered a 3-0 (11-5, 11-6, 11-0) win over Sri Lanka's Ravindu Laksiri in 25 minutes to reach the quarterfinals.Abhay will next face Japan's Ryunosuke in the last eight.Veer Chotrani also progressed after a five-game contest against Malaysia's Sanjay Jeeva. Veer won 3-2 (11-9, 8-11, 11-6, 15-17, 11-6) in a match that lasted one hour and nine minutes.He will face Pakistan's Irfan Muhammad in the quarterfinals.Earlier in the day, Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar advanced to the mixed doubles quarterfinals with a straight-games win over fellow Indians Suraj Chand and Shameena Riaz in the round of 16.The Indian pair, who won bronze at the Asian Championships, defeated Suraj and Shameena 11-7, 11-10.Joshna and Velavan will face the Philippines pair of David Pelino and Jemyca Aribado in the quarterfinals on Friday.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Baltimore heads to Brazil with something to prove against Dallas
articles.summary: Baltimore will attempt to rebound from its fourth-quarter collapse against New Orleans when it faces Dallas in a much hyped matchup in Brazil
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will travel to Brazil carrying more than passports, equipment, and the expectations that come with one of the NFL's most publicized games of the season. They will also carry questions about how they respond to adversity.

Baltimore surrendered an eight-point fourth-quarter lead in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints . The Ravens will attempt to prevent that collapse from becoming a trend when they face the Dallas Cowboys at Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

The Ravens led New Orleans 17-9 entering the fourth quarter but were outscored 15-0 over the final period. Baltimore produced only three second-half points, committed costly penalties and failed to capitalize on multiple possessions that reached Saints territory.

Lamar Jackson 's final pass was intercepted after the Ravens advanced to the New Orleans 37-yard line, ending their last opportunity to force overtime.

One loss does not define Baltimore's season. How the Ravens respond could reveal much more about their direction under Jesse Minter.

Baltimore handed Derrick Henry the football only 16 times against New Orleans despite playing with a lead for most of the afternoon. He finished with 68 yards and a touchdown as the Ravens ran just 22 times. Dallas enters Week 3 allowing 173.5 rushing yards per game. That creates an obvious opportunity for Baltimore to recommit to its most physical offensive player. A productive running game would keep the Ravens ahead of the chains while limiting possessions for Dak Prescott and Dallas' explosive offense.

The defense faces a more dangerous challenge.

The Cowboys responded to their season-opening loss by defeating Washington 37-20. Prescott completed 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns, while CeeDee Lamb produced eight receptions for 153 yards and two scores. Baltimore's secondary cannot afford the coverage breakdowns or extended drives that helped New Orleans complete its comeback. The Ravens must pressure Prescott without losing track of Lamb and Dallas' other playmakers.

The international stage adds to the spotlight.

Sunday's game will be the NFL's first regular-season contest in Rio de Janeiro. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at the historic Maracanã Stadium. The travel, unfamiliar surroundings, and heightened attention will test Baltimore's preparation. The Ravens cannot allow those circumstances to become distractions. Baltimore is 1-1, and there is no reason for panic. A disciplined performance against Dallas would turn Week 2 into a correctable setback. Another late collapse would create more difficult questions heading into October.

articles.title: Ravens’ stingy run defense meets a Cowboys ground game in trouble
articles.summary: Baltimore allows 83.5 rushing yards per game. Dallas averages 67.5, putting pressure on Dak Prescott in Brazil
articles.body:
Baltimore's run defense can shape Sunday's game in Brazil before Dak Prescott has a chance to get comfortable throwing the football.

The Ravens have allowed 167 rushing yards in two games, an average of 83.5 , while Dallas has gained just 135 , or 67.5 per game . The Cowboys are averaging 3.5 yards per carry and have produced only seven rushing first downs. Baltimore has permitted 3.6 yards per attempt, though opponents have scored three rushing touchdowns. The Ravens have contained yardage; they still have work to do near the goal line.

That distinction matters against Dallas. The Cowboys have shown they can score without a productive rushing attack. Prescott threw four touchdowns in their Week 2 win over Washington, distributing the ball to a receiving group led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . Stopping the run alone will not stop that offense.

It could, however, narrow Dallas' options. Second-and-long and third-and-long would give Baltimore's pass rush more chances to attack Prescott. The Ravens have five sacks through two games, but the Cowboys have allowed only two. If Baltimore lets Dallas stay ahead of the chains, Prescott could continue working from a clean pocket.

The Ravens are looking to rebound from a loss in which New Orleans erased a fourth-quarter deficit. A strong run game would put Baltimore in favorable situations throughout the game. Finishing those possessions with stops, particularly in scoring territory, is the next step.

articles.title: Dodgers’ Breakout Star Tabbed As Final Hitter In Federal Gambling Investigation
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ outfield slugger is named in documents pertaining to a looming trial.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are getting a key piece of their lineup back at an important time of the season. Andy Pages returned from the injured list Tuesday to resume his role in the outfield as Los Angeles prepares for the postseason.

"Pages will make his return to the Dodgers after missing more than a month of action while recovering from surgery to address a left hand fracture," CBS Sports reported . "Once activated, Pages will likely take over as the Dodgers' everyday center fielder, pushing Tommy Edman back to second base and Alex Freeland into a bench role.

The timing of Pages' return comes at an important time for the Dodgers, who will be hoping he can recreate the World Series heroics that saw him make a stunning catch to overcome the Toronto Blue Jays last year. But it also comes alongside a more unexpected connection to one of Major League Baseball's biggest ongoing controversies.

Los Angeles Dodgers Slugger Andy Pages Plays Key Role In Pitch Rigging Case

Federal prosecutors have identified a pitch thrown to Pages in 2025 as the final one on a list of 18 throws at the center of their gambling case involving Cleveland Guardians closer Emmanuel Clase .

Prosecutors are focused on 18 pitches from 17 games ahead of the trial, according to the documents reviewed by ESPN's David Purdum . A pitch thrown to Andy Pages on May 28, 2025, in the ninth inning of a three-run loss to the Guardians in Cleveland is the most recent item on the list, according to Purdum.

Clase allegedly intended for the pitch to be a ball, but Pages swung at it and missed, turning the pitch into a strike.

Pages is not accused of participating in the alleged gambling scheme. Instead, prosecutors are expected to point to his at-bat against Clase in allegations that he and teammate Luis Ortiz had informed bettors of the velocity and results of their pitches in advance.

"The government will only seek to prove that for one or more of approximately 18 of Clase's pitches, and for two of Ortiz's pitches, the defendants provided advance inside information about their pitches to others, who bet on them," U.S. attorney Joseph Nocella wrote, per Purdum.

Los Angeles Dodgers, Andy Pages At-Bat Becomes Central To Looming Federal Trial

Alongside Pages, pitches thrown to several prominent MLB hitters are listed in the documents obtained by Purdum.

Jury selection for the trial is expected to begin in November.

"If convicted, each defendant faces a maximum sentence of 20 years' imprisonment on the wire fraud conspiracy count, 20 years' imprisonment on the honest services wire fraud conspiracy count, five years' imprisonment on the conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery count, and 20 years' imprisonment on the money laundering conspiracy count," the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York announced .

articles.title: Bayern Munich star Harry Kane wants to be remembered for his character, not just his football
articles.summary: FC Bayern’s number 9 exudes class on and off the pitch
articles.body:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is the definition of a complete player: he can score, he can pass, he can assist, he can defend, he can cross and do so much more. Despite the qualities that he possesses, the England star wants to be remembered for other things on top of that.

"I want to be remembered as someone who puts the team above everything and who respects his teammates," Kane said in an interview with the Telegraph (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). "You're never bigger than your team, club or country. I've always worked hard, in silence and without showing off. Despite the highs and lows, I've always believed in myself and worked twice as much. I just want to keep doing it for as long as possible."

In a world where footballers would make everything about themselves, Kane never subscribed to that mindset. He has always made it a point to be a team player, to improve himself, and to simply enjoy the game as much as possible.

articles.title: Eagles Reunion Gives Zach Ertz One Final Shot at Incredible Franchise Record
articles.summary: Zach Ertz spent nearly five years stuck 10 catches behind Harold Carmichael in the Eagles' record book. He probably had a better chance of running into Carmi...
articles.body:
Zach Ertz spent nearly five years stuck 10 catches behind Harold Carmichael in the Eagles' record book. He probably had a better chance of running into Carmichael at the grocery store than catching another pass for Philadelphia .

Now Ertz is back with the team that traded him in 2021, and a record that seemed destined to stay out of reach is suddenly up for grabs. Philadelphia certainly didn't bring him back for a nostalgia tour. The Eagles are running out of healthy tight ends, and Ertz knows a thing or two about playing the position.

Eleven catches would put him atop the franchise's all-time receptions list. Getting them might be a little more complicated.

Eagles Reunion Gives Zach Ertz One Final Shot at Incredible Franchise Record

Carmichael finished his Eagles career with 589 receptions. Ertz had 579 when Philadelphia shipped him to the Arizona Cardinals in October 2021, ending a run that included three Pro Bowls and a Super Bowl championship.

He'd already caught the go-ahead touchdown against the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII. He'd also put together a ridiculous 116-catch season in 2018 , setting what was then an NFL record for tight ends.

Philadelphia handed the position to Goedert, and Ertz went about extending his career elsewhere. He spent time with Arizona and Washington before a torn ACL interrupted his latest chapter.

There wasn't much reason to think he'd ever get another opportunity to chase Carmichael. The Eagles had moved on, Ertz was getting older, and the record wasn't going anywhere.

Eagles Turn to a Familiar Face After Injuries Pile Up

Goedert's injury was bad enough. With Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers also unavailable, Philadelphia found itself digging through the available tight ends before September was even over.

The Eagles signed him to their practice squad Tuesday, although nobody should expect him to walk through the door and immediately start playing 60 snaps. He's 35, coming off major knee surgery and hasn't played a regular-season game since tearing his ACL with Washington.

That's quite a bit of rust to knock off.

Still, Philadelphia doesn't need Ertz to catch another 116 passes. A couple of third-down conversions, some help in the red zone and a veteran who knows where he's supposed to line up would be a welcome start.

The interesting part is what happens if Goedert misses several games.

Ertz wouldn't need a particularly heavy workload to catch 11 passes over a few weeks. Of course, that's assuming his knee holds up, he gets promoted to the active roster and Jalen Hurts actually looks his way.

A few assumptions for a guy who hasn't played in months.

Ertz Could Leave Philadelphia With One More Record

The Eagles host Chicago on Monday night, giving Ertz a few days to get reacquainted with an organization he once helped deliver its first Super Bowl championship.

His stay could be brief. Goedert will eventually return, and Philadelphia isn't going to keep its younger tight ends on the sidelines just so Ertz can chase a record.

But consider where he was a week ago. Ertz was unemployed, recovering from knee surgery and watching the Eagles play without him. Now he's back in Philadelphia with a legitimate opportunity to pass Carmichael.

And wouldn't it be something if a franchise record that survived more than four decades finally fell because Philadelphia couldn't keep its tight ends healthy?

articles.title: Hibs appoint Dutchman Reedijk as new manager
articles.summary: Former Beveren head coach Marink Reedijk vows to develop a "brave, intense and committed" Hibernian team after becoming the club's new manager.
articles.body:
Former Beveren head coach Marink Reedijk has vowed to develop a "brave, intense and committed" Hibernian team after becoming the club's new manager.

The Dutchman, 35, replaces David Gray, who was sacked eight days ago after a difficult start to the term for the Scottish Premiership outfit.

Reedijk has spent the last two seasons with Beveren, earning promotion to the top flight last season after an unbeaten campaign before leaving in the summer.

He previous worked in academy roles at Ajax and West Bromwich Albion, and in with the senior teams at KSV Roeselare, Vitesse and RSCA Futures.

Hibs say Reedijk - who is "honoured" to be appointed - arrives with a reputation for attacking football and building a strong team culture.

"I can feel the ambition and see the clarity of what the club is trying to achieve," he said. "That was a big part of what attracted me here.

"I want us to be an assertive team. A team that gives everything, plays with purpose and gives our supporters something to really get behind."

Reedijk will be assisted by Rogier Molhoek at Easter Road, with the club hailing his arrival as "an exciting moment".

The Edinburgh outfit are currently 10th in the Premiership, with two wins from their opening seven matches, and endured a gut-wrenching Conference League exit.

Under Gray, they finished third in 2024/25 and fifth last term, with the departed manager also leading them to November's League Cup semi-finals, where they will face city rivals Hearts.

Sporting director Malky Mackay insists Reedijk's recruitment is not about "changing the direction" of their footbal strategy, but is about "continuing to evolve it".

"We believe Marink is an excellent fit to take the team forward," he added.

"We began this process with a clear idea of the type of team we want to continue to build and the qualities we wanted from our next manager. Marink's philosophy, his work with players and his leadership style are strongly aligned with that.

"His teams are proactive, high energy and dynamic. What also stands out is his ability to develop individuals and create a strong collective environment."

Ross: Decent appointment, time will tell if it's the right one. His credentials and philosophy sits well with me and what we want to achieve. Welcome and all the best.

Lee: Another young manager! Let's get behind him, and the team and give him a chance to show what he is capable of. I hope it works out, because if it doesn't, beyond the dugout is where the spotlight should be.

Tony: Brilliant, good to have someone in quickly. Not a great knowledge of the guy but from what I've read he likes an attacking team with wingers so that's a positive. Will be good to see what he can do with the current squad. It probably won't solve it quickly but let's see.

articles.title: AEW’s Thekla on Unfiltered Promos, Growing Popularity & Going ‘All Out’
articles.summary: Plus, the 'Toxic Spider' also talks music, art and her surprising TV show binges.
articles.body:
Just as Spider-Man continues to rule the box office, one "Toxic Spider" looks to return to the top of the All Elite Wrestling food chain. Thekla's web of violence and carnage has made the Austrian a breakout star. She'll take on Willow Nightingale on September 26 at All Out for a shot at the Women's Championship, currently held by Mercedes Moné .

For Thekla, the pay-per-view event isn't just about being next in line at WrestleDream . The foul-mouthed member of the Triangle of Madness wants to defeat Nightingale after she dethroned her for the Women's Championship at Redemption in July.

Despite the performer's underhanded tactics and vulgarity that probably put the TBS and TNT censors on high alert, the rule-breaker continues to grow in popularity. The unpredictable livewire has connected with the audience in ways maybe she even didn't expect. Though in the world of pro wrestling precedence does exist with rebel "Stone Cold" Steve Austin a shining example.

Here Thekla sits down with a Capri Sun in hand to talk about her recent success and why what we've seen is only the beginning.

You're this despicable person on television, yet people have gravitated to you. What do you make of this?

Thekla: Yeah, I don't know what's wrong with people. Honestly, I always thought I was living on my own planet, with my own sense of humor and the things I like that not everybody else needs to like. Maybe people gravitate towards me being people who are just unapologetically themselves. I think that's something that everybody strives to be, themselves, but it's really hard. I guess that's kind of something that's entertaining to people, when they see somebody that is full-fledged whatever it is I'm f*cking doing, I don't know.

How much freedom do you typically have when it comes to what you say on the TV shows?

Apart from the usual stuff they try to make sure I don't say on TV? It's very hard for me not to say on TV that whole list of words that we get fined for. Other than that, I get to say pretty much what I want. I take a lot of inspiration from what I really like, and what I really feel, and what I think about people and myself. I get a lot more creativity than I thought I ever would. I get to choose more stuff than I probably should as well. So I get away with a lot of sh*t.

I have to ask. What's in those cups that you're drinking while cutting those promos?

That's a dumb b*tch question. Next question.

Okay, we'll keep that a mystery. But where do you find inspiration? I watch a lot of movies. I love a good movie and going to the cinema. I like books. I read a lot of autobiographies of people I find interesting. I'm a huge music person. I listen to a lot of music and the type of music then kind of inspires the way I feel. Right now, I'm in my Hispanic, Latin reggaeton phase, which might be surprising to some people. Then again, if you watch the way I'm having matches right now and dancing around the ring, maybe not. I'm just constantly listening to music in my head in general. My heroes are people like Iggy Pop, Lou Reed , you know, kind of like 60s, 70s, punk idols. I also love unapologetic characters. I like television. I'm also a big Quentin [Tarantino] fan. I'm watching a lot of old gangster movies from the 70s now. The type of Godfather type of stuff.

I am binging Curb Your Enthusiasm , watching the last stuff I haven't seen yet. I've been turned on to It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia a little bit. That's where the chaos comes from. I like a good chaos show.

How is it getting acclimated living in the United States and traveling throughout the country?

Well, what I don't love is the time zones. Americans, you got to get a hold of that because it's very confusing to people who are from here too. I love traveling. It's just cool. We did that Dynamite in the Midwest, and that part of America I haven't seen too much of yet. When we have two extra days in between Collision and Dynamite . Where we get to rent a car, drive around, and eat, and find a little shack on the side of the road. I love to go to a dive bar and stuff like that. I like the trashy Americana stuff too. Like broken blinking neon lights at night. Getting into wrestling, one of my number one things was that I wanted to travel and see the world, and I'm finally getting to do that. And I'm finally figuring out a way to not only go from airport to airport and hotel to hotel. Taking out big chunks and doing it right in a way where I can I feel like I'm getting to experience America, which is a f*ckin huge and cool and diverse country. It's insane.

Do you have a go-to travel partner or do you travel solo?

I mostly travel with The Dogs. We go way back because we were kind of a gang in Japan. Coming up in New Japan Pro-Wrestling and me with Stardom alongside Clark Connors, Gabe Kidd, David Finlay, those are the guys. It's also the smart bi*ches. You'll find me at the hotel bar with Lita Kross and Megan Bayne.

Speaking of Stardom, you're also the Artist of Stardom Champions with other Triangle of Madness members Julia Hart and Skye Blue. What has it been like seeing those two gain some fandom in Japan?

That has been huge for me. That is one of the main reasons I even went back to Japan after my one-year hiatus. It can be very hard when you don't have the backstory and the connections. For those girls, to make sh*t happen, because there's a language barrier and everything. It's really cool that we made it happen. That we got the titles. That Julia got to do the [5★STAR Grand Prix] is huge. I've still met so many legends. They're like, "I've never been to Japan. That's always been my dream. And Julia, especially, has been getting over so much. It's insane. We had another title match there two weeks ago. I know how they know me there, but just coming in and everybody just yelling, Julia, Julia. They're obsessed with her. I'm really happy. I'm really happy because I know I partly made that happen. I got, not only the connection to people who run sh*t, but also the story to make it make sense.

We're seeing returning faces like Britt Baker with other names potentially coming in like free agents Kairi Sane. What do you make of the landscape of the women's division right now in AEW?

I always like new faces coming in. I still consider myself a new face somehow. It has only been a little bit over a year for me. I'm a huge fan of people just going from one territory to the other, like in the old days. I'm very excited to see who's gonna step up, you know? Kairi has been the talk of the town. I'm only going to believe it once I see it. For the fans, it's always cool to see a new matchup. We'll see. Let's keep our fingers crossed. Let us see if we can pice it up a little bit.

This weekend you have your big match against Willow. You're building up this great rivalry. What has been like to work with her?

With Willow, we're seeing a different side of her. I've been known to bring out the worst in people, especially with a huge smiley babyface like Willow is. It's cool to see that f*ck you aggression come out. I don't like this b*tch, and I'm totally cool with that. That's the kind of energy I like. I think a little negativity, a little hate in the ring is good because it's about conflict. It's about not liking each other. I don't love a good handshake before a match. F*ck that. Let's make it messy. I think me and Willow, we might be a forever feud. That's the kind of stuff I like.

What does that potential match against Mercedes Moné mean to you?

it would obviously be a huge one. I've seen how people have been looking forward to it. A lot of people thought this was the match they were going to get to see at All In . When it happens, it's going to be big. It's going to be interesting. I know it is going to happen. When? Probably WrestleDream , maybe not, you know? Like, b*tches keep on getting hurt left and right. You never f*cking know. I'm hoping for the best, you know?

You have so many interests. Outside of wrestling, you also have been involved with music in groups like Death Row Groupies. Will we ever see you perform on the AEW shows, maybe as part of your entrance like Chris Jericho has done with Fozzy? Yeah, that's a hundred percent something I want to see. I have no idea where our drummer is. He might be dead in a ditch somewhere. You never know with my friends. I haven't heard from him in years. My other friend is somewhere stuck in Vienna. Who f*cking knows, I'm definitely going to go back to making music at some point. Whenever I get the opportunity, I think about doing an entrance with one of my past bands. Death Row Groupies isn't the only band I ever had. I'm also super interested in starting some new stuff. We got so many cool people who are capable of playing instruments. Maybe there's a Brody King-Thekla connection coming up sometime in the future. Who f*cking knows?

I'm also excited about seeing your work in the "House Show: Power, Spectacle, and Pro Wrestling" exhibit at the Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg next year. What can we expect?

I'm currently setting up my new studio here in Arizona. I'm planning on producing some new works, which people who know my art have been anticipating for a long time. I'm not sure yet what the medium is going to be. I'm probably going to start drawing a lot, and I'm still thinking about bringing out a new, um, art book after the last one ["K.O. City"] I did two years ago. So I've got a lot of unused material, and I've got some new ideas. That might be a surprise thing that I'm just gonna drop before the end of the year.

Have you ever got commissioned by Tony Khan or another one of the wrestlers to do a piece?

I have actually. Renee [Paquette] just recently asked me if I was open to doing commissions. I usually don't do commissions because my mind doesn't work like that. It's a lot. It's already f*cking hard to be creative, and then being creative under certain circumstances, is even worse. And I don't really care too much about the money aspect of it. Unless she gives me a really good idea, and it's like, "You know, that would be cool." And I say, "F*ck yeah, that's a great idea." Then I'd be willing to do whatever, we settle on. I might be doing a big piece for her [and Jon Moxley], actually, for their house.

You have a busy couple of months coming up. What do you want to see from your career and AEW beyond the obvious winning the championship again? See, that's hard for me because I came in so hot, and I've already done so many things. The only thing they took away from me was All In . And I'm kind of happy with that because otherwise I would have ticked all the boxes already. All the boxes, except for like coming up with cool ways to do an entrance and sh*t like that. I was holding the big one for seven months, I think? I already had really cool interactions with some of the best bi*ches we have on the roster. I remember they bring in stuff with people who are not wrestlers. Before I came to AEW, they did a feature with Doja Cat for one of her songs, and they had this little AEW music video. So I'd always be down to work with somebody who I mutually respect. That could be cool. As for wrestling, I got to do the strap match, which was the first women's strap match we had in AEW. That was sick. I could totally see myself doing a dog collar type of match. Those kinds of special rules, like first blood and that type of stuff. For that, I need a good feud. I don't like to get messy without a good story.

There is the potential of Blood & Guts again.

Exactly, exactly. Who knows? From how well it went last year, good or bad, I'm not sure. I still have some scars here. I just got a tetanus shot because we might be doing Blood & Guts again. You know, I'm not taking any chances, motherf*cker. I love my job. Let's put it that way. F*cking love my job.

articles.title: Presidents Cup Needs Fix After US Streak Dominates
articles.summary: The Presidents Cup struggles with predictability as the US dominates. Seven structural changes could save the event from becoming a mere corporate retreat.
articles.body:
The golf world gathers at the revamped Medinah this week, yet the air feels heavy with a lack of suspense. Fans are asked to pretend the event carries real competitive weight, but the reality is stark. The Americans hold ten of the top fifteen players in the world, a statistic highlighted by Data Golf. In contrast, the International Team boasts only one player in that elite tier, Si Woo Kim. This massive gap turns the biennial event into something resembling a corporate retreat rather than a true battle.

The United States has won ten consecutive Presidents Cups, holding a crushing 13-1-1 record over the years. The International Team's only outright victory dates back so far that many current competitors were not even alive when it happened. The event exists largely so the PGA Tour can maintain a store-brand version of the Ryder Cup, but the luster has faded fast.

While the tournament has produced memorable moments, like one of Tiger Woods' nastiest club twirls, these flashes do not fix the fundamental problem. Fans assume the US will win, and they are almost always right. No amount of marketing can change that mindset. MyGolfSpy argues that the format needs significant structural changes to create a closer competition and give the event a distinct identity.

The first major issue involves player eligibility. Because the PGA Tour operates the Presidents Cup, LIV golfers have been ineligible to compete. This rule has specifically prevented the International Team from selecting top talents like Joaquin Niemann and Cameron Smith. Without these players, the International side is severely weakened before the first ball is even struck.

The absence of these global stars creates a lopsided field that fails to engage the average viewer. The current roster selection process ignores the best players available, focusing instead on tour affiliation rather than pure skill.

Fixing this event requires bold moves that address the root causes of the imbalance. The most obvious solution is to let the best players compete, regardless of which tour they play on. This change would naturally solve many of the current issues before the next edition of the tournament takes place.

The International Team needs a realistic chance to win, and that chance disappears when top-tier talent is banned from the field. The current 13-1-1 record shows that the status quo is broken. A true competition requires both sides to have a legitimate shot at victory.

If the format remains unchanged, the event will continue to feel like a formality rather than a highlight of the golf calendar. The identity crisis must end, or the tournament risks becoming irrelevant to fans who crave genuine suspense and high-stakes drama.

articles.title: The “massive sign” that Chelsea already have their key attacking player in place
articles.summary: Chelsea striker Joao Pedro has been one of the best signings in the league in the last couple of years, and we can’t wait to see him in action again.If you e...
articles.body:
Chelsea striker Joao Pedro has been one of the best signings in the league in the last couple of years, and we can't wait to see him in action again.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Carlton Cole has been speaking about Joao Pedro and the potential impact he could have on Chelsea and their season.

"When he's not playing, you can see the effect it has on the team," the ex-Chelsea striker said in quotes picked up by Goal.com.

"So that's a massive sign that he's a big part of the set-up that [Xabi] Alonso's building. And I'm looking at it, and I think he's one of those players that could actually get into high double figures this season if used correctly and stays fit. He's one of the ones to watch out for this season, definitely."

Joao Pedro need Chelsea colleagues to step up to his level

Joao Pedro (Photo by Chris Lee/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

High double figures would imply that JP is going to score 80 or 90 goals this season, and despite his quality we can't quite see that. But we know what Cole means. If the Brazilian can score 30 in all competitions, that would be a great return and mean Chelsea have a number 9 with the consistency needed to take this team to the very top level – if the rest of the team can just sort itself out.

Chelsea can't unilaterally recall Alejandro Garnacho in January, but that doesn't mean he won't be coming back in the winter market.

Links to a Man City defender from Chelsea are pretty interesting – but we will have to go a long way before we believe them.

articles.title: Frosinone chief reveals why Celtic’s Fares Ghedjemis transfer pursuit collapsed
articles.summary: Frosinone sporting director Renzo Castagnini has revealed why Celtic’s summer pursuit of Fares Ghedjemis ultimately failed despite the winger wanting to leav...
articles.body:
Frosinone sporting director Renzo Castagnini has revealed why Celtic's summer pursuit of Fares Ghedjemis ultimately failed despite the winger wanting to leave the Italian club.

Fares Ghedjemis of Algeria is seen in action during an international friendly match between Algeria and Guatemala at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on March 27, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

Celtic spent much of the transfer window attempting to bring the Algerian to Glasgow after initially missing out on his signature in January.

Martin O'Neill publicly admitted the Hoops had a "very strong" interest in Ghedjemis, but Frosinone stood firm despite approaches for one of their prized assets.

Ghedjemis had rejected the opportunity to join Celtic in January before helping Frosinone secure promotion to Serie A, but his position had changed by the summer and he was open to moving on.

However, a significant development behind the scenes at Frosinone altered the club's financial position and removed their need to cash in on the winger.

Speaking to Radio Sportiva, Castagnini said: "Ghedjemis wanted to leave, and I believe that when a player has the opportunity to improve, it's right that he shows it.

"When the Clara Vista fund came in, since we no longer needed to sell players, it was decided that Ghedjemis would stay with us.

"We're working on his new contract, so we're satisfied. We're doing things properly and calmly."

Frosinone president Maurizio Stirpe had previously insisted the offers received for Ghedjemis did not meet the club's valuation, with Celtic and Rangers eventually dropping out of the race as the Serie A side refused to budge.

articles.title: ‘Performative’ Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon ripped by ex-ESPN personality
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is facing criticism for her sideline antics during games.
articles.body:
If you're tuning into an Indianapolis Colts game, you never know what to expect to see on the field, but you know what you will see on the sideline: Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon .

Irsay-Gordon has become one of the most involved and present NFL owners since stepping into the owner role following the death of her father, Jim Irsay , in May 2025, and she has become a staple on the sideline during games.

On game days, you will see Irsay-Gordon patrolling the sideline with a headset so she can be in touch with communication between the staff, while holding a notepad to jot down her observations during the action. She also pops into team meetings.

Irsay-Gordon believes that learning the minor details of day-to-day operations helps her make informed decisions about how the franchise should move.

Oct 5, 2025; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon walks the sideline during the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Christine Tannous-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

"I think one of the things that I learned in going through, even as back as when we hired Chuck Pagano (in 2012), is that sort of accelerated my, ' I need to learn more about this, ' I need to be able to say, is this person full of BS? Do they even know what they're talking about?," she said in an interview with the team's website. "And I think one of the things that being on the headset has really helped me learn is to the question earlier, it's such a complex organism of football team and how it operates.

"You could say, 'Oh, that person ran that route wrong.' When you learn to find, 'Oh, someone tagged the wrong wide receiver, and it wasn't really the player's fault – it was the person that called it.' I think that's been very valuable, because it also helps us be able to know where do we need to make tweaks, what resources do we need, what do we need to fix. So much of it comes down to just how we operate and how things work and the headsets – I would suggest it for anyone else that has to pay coaches and GMs millions and millions of dollars. It helps you make a less expensive mistake potentially."

While Colts fans will love her dedication to the team, not everyone is on board. Former ESPN personality Ryen Russillo sounded off on the latest episode of The Ryen Russillo, calling Irsay-Gordon's actions "performative."

Ryen Russillo Calls Out 'Performative' Carlie Irsay-Gordon

"I want to see Carly Irsay's notes. I want to know what these notes are. It's very performative to me. I think her announcement is performative to the Colts fans that want her to be the hero for a team that is going through a disappointing run," Russillo said during his rant. "People could say that I'm only saying it because she's a woman, which would be total bullshit because Boston made fun of Robert Kraft forever because he brought a stopwatch to a workout.

"He walked around with a stopwatch and was manually timing people at workouts. When I see her do it, I want to know what, what are you writing down? Yeah. That's it. What are you writing down so that we have a better sense of what it is you're actually evaluating? Share the notes."

Russillo caught some immediate backlash in the comments section for his stance, with many praising Irsay-Gordon for her attention to detail and involvement in making sure the team is set up for the most success.

If the Colts can reach the playoffs for the first time since the 2020 season, it will be well worth the investment she has made in the day-to-day operations. And, at the end of the day, it's better to have an owner who cares rather than someone who is hands-off and just there to make money.

Carlie Irsay-Gordon, principal owner and CEO of the Indianapolis Colts, is photographed Thursday, Sept 25, 2025, in the trophy room at the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center in Indianapolis. Irsay-Gordon is holding a helmet worn by former Indianapolis Colts player Robert Mathis .
